intro_md: 📖 **9 min.** An email from Nam's little sister, Linh, in Hanoi. Look at the four chunks, then read the email once without going back.

parts.title: An email from Linh
parts.md:
**Four chunks you'll meet in this email:**

| Phrase | 🖼️ Picture it (literal) | So it means… |
|---|---|---|
| *to be honest* | You open a door and show someone the whole room – nothing is hidden. | I'll tell you the real truth now. |
| *lose your voice* | You shout all day. Then you open your mouth, and only air comes out – the voice has "gone". | You can't speak (or only whisper) because your throat is tired or ill. |
| *can't wait to* | A child stands at the door, jumping up and down, and can't stay still while waiting. | You are very excited to do something. |
| *take care of yourself* | You hold a cup that can break, and you look after it gently. | Look after your health and don't get too tired. |

👉 *To be honest, I don't like coffee. · He lost his voice at the football match. · I can't wait to see the sea. · Take care of yourself this winter.*

![Linh's classroom](data/img/w1/d14-linh.webp)

> **From:** Linh · **To:** Nam · **Subject:** Hello from Hanoi!
>
> Hi Nam,
>
> How are you? I'm writing this email in English because it's good practice for me. As you know, I started my new job on Monday. I'm a teacher at a primary school now!
>
> To be honest, I was very nervous before my first lesson. I have 35 children in my class, and they are all eight years old. When I walked in, they were all shouting, so I just stood there for a minute. Then I clapped my hands, and a small girl at the front said, "Teacher, you look scared!" Everyone laughed, and I laughed too.
>
> The children are lovely, but they never stop talking. By Wednesday I had lost my voice, so I taught with a whiteboard and lots of drawings. Yesterday the children said my drawings look like potatoes. Maybe they are right.
>
> Now some news from home. Mum asks every day, "Is Nam eating properly?" Please send her a photo of your dinner. Dad says hello and wants to know if you have bought a warm coat yet.
>
> And I have a big question: does it really rain every day in Manchester? My students think England is always grey, and I want to tell them the truth!
>
> I can't wait to visit you one day. Maybe next summer, if I save enough money. Until then, take care of yourself, eat some vegetables and sleep enough.
>
> Lots of love,
> Linh
>
> P.S. Please write back soon. I miss you!
